definition: Neophyte means someone who is new to or inexperienced in an activity.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word neophyte. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know neophyte should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Every summer the observatory adopts a few neophytes, teaching them to tell a satellite's steady drift from a meteor's streak.
A newcomer is only new to the room, not to the craft — a transfer student can be a newcomer and the best player in the league — while a neophyte is new to the whole practice itself.
Greenhorn goes further than neophyte — the neophyte is new to the craft; the greenhorn is so visibly raw that the whole room can spot it.

Rookie is the locker-room word for the learning stage, and it belongs to paid jobs and teams — the first year on the force, the first season in the league. Neophyte covers the same stage anywhere at all: forums, hobby clubs, and print, in slightly more formal dress.

A first-timer has made exactly one attempt — one race run, one loaf baked — so the word counts tries, not stages. A neophyte is at a stage of learning: still new to the whole practice, however many early attempts and lessons that stage already contains.
